children: Growing uncertainty surrounding the timing of OpenAI’s
public debut is adding pressure to SoftBank’s
upcoming listing of its U.S. data center developer, SB Energy

People familiar with the matter say SoftBank is seeking a valuation of roughly $50 billion for the unit, which has yet to bring a single data center online, in an IPO expected to raise between $5B and $7B within the coming weeks.

SB Energy represents SoftBank founder Masayoshi Son’s core infrastructure bet to capture surging artificial intelligence demand. The company boasts a massive $439B contract backlog, primarily covering 8.8 gigawatts of data center capacity tied to long-term leases, putting it second only to CoreWeave in third-party compute development.

However, because its major developments (including a massive 8GW campus in Ohio) remain under construction, $357B of that contracted revenue is only expected to be recognized from 2034 onwards. In the first half of this year, SB Energy generated just $138.7M in revenue, mostly from its legacy solar operations, alongside an operating loss of $551.6M.

The company’s prospects are tightly intertwined with OpenAI and Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA), both of which will hold equity stakes in the listed entity. OpenAI serves as the primary tenant for SB Energy's major pipeline projects, while Nvidia has provided a $105 billion guarantee for the initial phase of the Ohio buildout, the report noted.

SB Energy explicitly warned in its prospectus that its near-term financial health and project financing remain heavily dependent on OpenAI's continued performance. Market analysts and investors note that the listing faces valuation hurdles due to high customer concentration and immense capital requirements.

As per the report, SB Energy estimates it must fund more than $170B in capital expenditure to construct its project pipeline. To maintain its typical 10% equity stake in project financing, analysts estimate SB Energy will need to secure an additional $7B in equity beyond the IPO proceeds, alongside substantial debt.
Despite these financial demands, SoftBank remains confident in securing backing based on Son's track record with major public listings.

title: OpenAI IPO delay escalates pressure on SoftBank’s $50B SB Energy listing
